observed_problem.surface: Active Path Discovery fresh iPhone ZIP
observed_problem.symptom: Fresh scan succeeded but carried an old A-003 manifest SHA and five false current 412 blockers sourced from static comments/output-only filenames.
observed_problem.proven_code_gap: The scanner sourced integrity identity from pmp_route_guardian_v22_receipt in localStorage and its generic lexical extractor treated comment/output strings as runtime dependencies.

repair.manifest_binding: Fetch pmp-runtime-integrity-manifest-v1.json with no-store during the exact scan, hash exact response bytes with SHA-256, parse runtime source-set identity, and bind the evidence to requested scan_id.
repair.reference_truth: Strip static comments before lexical discovery; explicit src/href/fetch/import/importScripts/Worker references remain strong; generic metadata.json, packet.json, and report.json basenames are ignored only when they are weak lexical strings.
repair.exporter_compatibility_binding: The existing 2.7 ZIP handoff behavior is unchanged; its exact expected scanner version/revision are aligned to 1.5.0 / 1.1.0 so fresh ZIP export consumes the repaired canonical scanner rather than rejecting it.

verification.browser_requirement: Seed a stale route-receipt manifest SHA, serve different manifest bytes, and prove the fresh report uses the served SHA while comment/output-only 412 endpoints are never requested and a real explicit fetch reference remains discoverable.

claim_ceiling: Repository repair only until applicable CI, merge, automatic A-003 reseal, Pages deployment, and a fresh iPhone Atlas ZIP prove the served seal binding and blocker classification.
